{{recipe}}

'''Bacalhau à zé do pipo''' is a traditional Portuguese cod dish. It can be confused with various other Portuguese dried/salted codfish recipes.

==Ingredients==

=== Mashed potatoes ===

* 500 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] (18 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] / 1.1 [[Cookbook:Pound|lbs]]) white or golden [[Cookbook:Potato|potatoes]]
* [[Cookbook:Milk|Milk]] (optional)
* [[Cookbook:Pepper|Black pepper]] (optional)
* [[Cookbook:Lemon Juice|Lemon juice]] (optional)
* [[Cookbook:Eggs|Eggs]] (optional)
* 100 g (3.5 oz) black [[Cookbook:Olive|olives]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]

=== Assembly ===
* 400 g (14 oz / 0.9 lb) [[Cookbook:Salting|salted]] dried [[Cookbook:Cod|cod]]
* Milk
* Salt
* [[Cookbook:Pepper|White pepper]]
* 200 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] (7 oz / ½ lb) of [[Cookbook:Onion|onions]]
* 5 g [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]] [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]]
* [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|Olive oil]]
* [[Cookbook:Mayonnaise|Mayonnaise]]

==Procedure==

=== Mashed potatoes ===

# [[Cookbook:Roasting|Roast]] the potatoes in the oven until tender. Cool slightly.
# [[Cookbook:Mashing|Mash]] the potatoes, mixing in the milk, pepper, lemon juice, and eggs, if using.
# Mix in the olives. Season with salt to taste.

=== Assembly ===
# Prepare the cod by leaving it for 24 hours in water, changing the water once or twice.
# After the 24 hour period is up, put the cod in a pot with milk.
# [[Cookbook:Boiling|Boil]] the cod until slightly cooked, then season with salt and pepper. The milk will make the fish soft.
# [[Cookbook:Slicing|Slice]] the onions into rings, and [[Cookbook:Frying|fry]] in pan with garlic and lots of olive oil until slightly browned.
# Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 220°C (425°F).
# Place the cod in the center of a [[Cookbook:Baking Dish|casserole or baking dish]].
# Surround the fish with 500 g of the mashed potatoes, then top it with the fried onion.
# Cover the onion with a thick layer of mayonnaise, and sprinkle bread crumbs all over.
# [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] until toasted on top.
# Serve with a green wine from the north of Portugal.
